name: BoosterHub
description: All-in-one software, accounting included, for US high-school booster clubs. The article says close to $1M ARR, 2 full-time staff, and about 600 programs. Company-stated. The article is not a product site.

mentions.evidence: Company-stated, from a Practical Founders article. Close to $1M ARR, 2 full-time staff, about 600 programs.
mentions.indieAngle: One kind of volunteer treasurer, one country, the books included.

whyItPrints: A booster club has to collect money, keep the books, and show parents where it went. Two people selling that to hundreds of clubs is the whole story in the article.
whyThisMatters:
A US high-school booster club collects money for the team and has to show parents where it went. BoosterHub is the software for that, and the accounting is included. A Practical Founders article says the yearly number is close to a million, with two full-time people and about six hundred programs. That is the company talking. It is not a Stripe connection. The article is not the product site.

Two people and hundreds of clubs is the part that makes it a note. I am not describing features the article did not list.

You pay so the treasurer is not a parent with a spreadsheet.

The clubs are the customer. Parents are not buying a login. Two full-time people is the staff count in the article, and I am not adding a third.

Accounting is included, which is the part a volunteer treasurer actually needs. The article calls it one system of record. I am not listing modules the piece never named. About six hundred programs is the reach they stated.
